Putting the same header inside the workspace is a different route: `connect` then resolves `workspace_local` to that project file. That is ordinary source, the same shape #3493 already keys, not a system header.

## Why a summary cannot paper over it

`canonical_external_callee` returns nothing for an unqualified name. C/C++ does not publish single-segment external owners (#2606). The bare-call arm records no reference text and no `ExactExternalCallProof`, so `synthetic_unmaterialized_external` mints no target. `procedure-effects` treats the site as an armless residual (#2579). No target-keyed summary can address it.

A follow-up also has to choose one pack label. `modeled_procedure_key_for_unit` labels a `.c` workspace function `cpp`. A `.c` semantic artifact is dialect `cpp-c`. No external key exists yet, so the split is not visible on a bound call, and the fix has to publish one label on purpose.

## Work

Publish a resolver-owned procedure key for the one file-scope function a compile-database-scoped header closure declares: declaring header, name, and written arity. Do not match the effect from the spelling. Until that key exists, #3457 stays open and ships no C specialization.

## 8. Draft approach comment

Landed as `ac4f88b730915d32ec5afb82e7fe341b4d023192`, which preserves the fix commit `cf51bdbd74d801fc426a246d22e5252e39c53cc1`. A C call to a function that a system or library header declares at file scope, such as POSIX `connect`, published no callee identity. The generated header pack dropped such declarations because nothing owned them, so a reviewed summary could never attach and every caller stayed open. The header pack now publishes each file-scope declaration under a module owner for its declaring header. A bare call in a `.c` file binds the one such function its compile-database header closure declares, at the written arity, and only when no workspace function of that name exists. The identity is the declaring header's include path without its extension, the name, the written arity and no receiver, labelled `cpp`, so a reviewed summary names it as `path: sys/socket.h`, `symbol: connect`. The generated-pack cache version moved from 29 to 30; no extraction epoch changed. With a reviewed network summary active, the issue's fixture and the plain-C POSIX and libcurl reproduction report a declared effect with exhaustive coverage, and eleven negative controls stay open with no effect. The route is C only: a C++ file calling the same `extern "C"` function stays open, because argument-dependent lookup could add another function the analyzer cannot rule out, and the C++ row depends on #3458. A call with an unprovable written arity, for example through a conditional macro, stays open pending #3676, and a name declared by two reached headers stays ambiguous. A same-named workspace function anywhere keeps the call open. Real glibc and libcurl headers still need parse recovery around unexpanded declaration macros, and quoted includes inside external headers are not followed, so those calls stay open for now.
